summary: As Trinity flies the helicopter away from the government building, Agent Smith shoots out of a shattered window, puncturing the rear hull so that "smoke and oil pour out like black blood." With the dying machine, Trinity throws it toward a nearby roof. Neo and Morpheus drop and roll free, but the rope snaps taut and yanks Neo toward the edge. Trinity lunges for the back door with her gun, grabs the rope, and fires to sever the cord just as the helicopter smashes blades-first into a glass skyscraper. Holding the rope, Trinity swings, connected to Neo, while the helicopter explodes. She bounces against a shatterproof window that spider-cracks as flames erupt behind her.

what_changes.before: In control, flying away from the building
what_changes.after: Forced into a desperate rescue, swinging from a rope after the helicopter is destroyed
what_changes.evidence: Trinity lunges for the back door, her gun in one hand, grabbing for the rope with the other

what_changes.before: Safely on the roof, trying to detach himself
what_changes.after: Yanked off his feet and dragged toward the edge by the falling helicopter
what_changes.evidence: The coils of slack snap taut, yanking Neo off his feet, dragging him with ferocious speed towards the edge

what_changes.after: Destroyed, crashing into a skyscraper and exploding
what_changes.evidence: Trinity fires, severing the cord from the helicopter, falling free of it as it SMASHES, blades first into a GLASS skyscraper

what_changes.before: Standing in the window, aiming his gun
what_changes.after: Having fired but failed to stop them, presumably still in the building
what_changes.evidence: Agent Smith stands in the shattered window, aiming his GUN out through the curtain of rain

event_hint.one_line: Trinity's escape helicopter is shot down, forcing a mid-air rescue that leaves the team stranded on a rooftop as the chopper explodes.

uncertain: Whether Agent Smith survives the helicopter gunfire from the previous scene or is a new instance
Whether Neo and Trinity end up in immediate danger after the window spider-cracks

minds.wants: To keep the machine airborne long enough to get Neo and Morpheus onto the roof, and then to not let the rope — and Neo — fall with the dying helicopter.
minds.feels: A rapid collapse of a plan she had under control into pure improvisation; the pilot's calculation (guide the parabola, trade the machine for the men) running straight into the raw refusal to let Neo be the thing that gets lost. Her "Shit-shit-no!" is the whole interior in one breath.
minds.shows: Only competent, violent action — throwing the helicopter toward the roof, lunging for the door, grabbing the rope, firing to sever the cord, riding the swing to the window. No panic on display, only reflex.
minds.basis: She narrates the crash as loss ('Shit-shit-no!') yet never stops executing — she guides the fall over the roof, then reaches for both gun and rope at once and cuts the cord at the last possible instant. Her belief about Neo is legible in the fact that she grabs the rope rather than letting go of the aircraft to save herself.

believes_about.belief: He is hers to pull out of the fall — that if she reaches and fires at the right instant, both of them survive.
believes_about.wrong_because: The physics nearly disproves her: the cord yanks Neo off his feet and flings him at the parapet, and only his own gutter-lever, not her grab, keeps him from going over. Her confidence in being his safety is real but not sufficient.

believes_about.belief: He is a threat that has been out-raced — the helicopter is already up and away when he reaches the window.
believes_about.wrong_because: He is still accurate enough to kill the aircraft ('PONK. PONK. PONK,' black blood), so her escape is not clean; she believes she's gotten clear when she has only traded a clean exit for a survivable catastrophe.

minds.wants: To get himself and Morpheus onto solid ground and free of the machine before the machine takes them with it.
minds.feels: The vertiginous flip from savior to liability. He has just, in the previous scene, flung himself into 'the wide blue empty space' to catch Morpheus and succeeded ('Gotcha!'); here the rope he trusted becomes the thing that snatches him off his feet and drags him toward the edge. The 'Uh-oh --' is the sound of control leaving his body.
minds.shows: Barely anything but reaction and reflex — clinging to Morpheus during the fall, rolling free, then scrambling to detach the harness, then being dragged and levering himself up on the gutter. He lets the near-disaster stay small ('Uh-oh').
minds.basis: His arc in this scene is passive-to-reactive: he 'tries to detach himself' while the rope goes slack, then is yanked off his feet and only saves himself by hitting the gutter and levering up. The contrast with sc-168, where he was the active leaper who caught Morpheus, is the whole reading.

believes_about.belief: It is his tether to safety — the same 'umbilical cord attached to a machine' he chose to clip onto in sc-168.
believes_about.wrong_because: In this scene the tether is exactly what endangers him; the slack snapping taut is the machine trying to take him into its death, so his trust in the line is momentarily misplaced.

believes_about.belief: She has the helicopter and the situation handled — she is the pilot, he is cargo.
believes_about.wrong_because: Not wrong in intent, but the machine is dying beyond her control; what actually saves him is Trinity severing the cord and his own body catching the gutter, not any continued mastery of the flight.

minds.wants: To get off the falling machine and onto the roof — to survive the extraction he committed to.
minds.feels: Little room for anything but pure physical will: he has just been shot in the leg (sc-168), was caught mid-fall by Neo, and is now dropping onto a roof. Whatever fear or assessment there is gets subordinated instantly to the roll and the landing.
minds.shows: Only the body — clinging during the fall, dropping and rolling free. No word, no look we are given.
minds.basis: The scene gives him no line and no reaction beyond 'drop safely, rolling free'; his leg wound from sc-168 means the safe landing is itself an effort he absorbs silently. There is no legible interior beyond survival-reflex here.

minds.wants: To stop the escape — to put a bullet through the helicopter and the people on it before it gets away.
minds.feels: The cold precision of the Agent who was, moments ago in sc-166 and sc-168, shot and thwarted (his 'No.' and his 'Nooo!'); here he converts that thwarting into a single effective act — he can't keep them, but he can destroy the machine. There is satisfaction in the puncturing, and a controlled fury underneath the stillness of his aim.
minds.shows: Absolute stillness and aim — 'stands in the shattered window, aiming his GUN out through the curtain of rain' — then the mechanical PONK of the rounds. No outburst now; the rage has been distilled into accuracy.
minds.basis: He is the last Agent standing (Jones and Brown were killed in sc-166; Smith himself was shot there and is either surviving or a fresh instance), and after Morpheus escaped his sweeping fire in sc-168, his only available win here is to kill the aircraft, which he does. The shift from 'Nooo!' to silent, effective shooting is the whole interior.

believes_about.belief: Neo is a program he can destroy by conventional means — put enough rounds into the machine and the problem ends.
believes_about.wrong_because: He is shooting at a man who is, by the story's shape, the One; the bullets destroy the helicopter and strand the team but do not end Neo, and this gap between 'kill the body/machine' and 'kill the One' is what will unravel Smith later.

believes_about.belief: That destroying the helicopter ends the chase — that they are now stranded and finished.
believes_about.wrong_because: They survive the fall and swing to safety; the escape continues to the subway (ev-029/ev-030), so his belief that he has closed the hunt is false — he has only forced them onto the next ground.

connects_back: sc-166: Neo mounts the .50 and fires through the window; the Agents go for their weapons and Smith is shot — this is the shot Smith answers here by shooting back out of that same shattered window.
sc-168: Neo clipped one rope-end to a bar and caught Morpheus mid-fall ('Gotcha!'); the very line he trusted now snatches him off the roof, paying that trust forward as danger.
sc-168: Morpheus was shot in the leg during his dive for the window, which is why his 'safe' roll onto the roof is a wounded man's landing, not an easy one.
sc-168: Smith's 'Nooo!' as Morpheus escaped his sweeping fire is the emotional debt he settles by puncturing the helicopter in this scene.
sets_up: The team stranded on a rooftop with their extraction destroyed, forcing Morpheus to arrange a new exit by phone — the rooftop regroup and the decision to route through the subway at State and Balbo (ev-029).
The Agents confirming the trace and escalating to a wider strike, which drives the chase toward the subway station (ev-030).
Trinity and Neo, alone together at the edge after surviving the fall, which sets the conditions for her confession of love in the phone booth (ev-030).
Smith's survival of the firefight and his fixation on Neo, which makes his reappearance as the subway threat possible (ev-030/ev-031).
Neo's repeated survival despite the physics being against him — a small installment toward the belief, tested and confirmed later, that he is more than the machine can kill (ev-031 onward).
dramatic_function: To convert a clean escape into a near-catastrophe that both raises the cost of the flight and re-pairs the team: it takes Neo from the triumphant rescuer of sc-168 and makes him the one who must be saved, binds him to Trinity through the rope she refuses to drop, and gives Smith a pyrrhic 'win' (destroying the machine) that strands the heroes and funnels them toward the subway — turning triumph into vulnerability so the chase can escalate.
